source.title: Large Language Models Show Signs of Alignment with Human Neurocognition During Abstract Reasoning
source.authors: Christopher Pinier; Sonia Acuna Vargas; Mariia Steeghs-Turchina; D. Matzke; Claire E. Stevenson; Michael D. Nunez

record.tranche_reason: The study compares representation geometries across several LLMs using RSA and a task-defined reference geometry, rather than directly testing whether pairwise distances between models become more alike with scale.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that task-optimal representations from all eight LLMs organize trials by abstract-pattern category, and reports a correlation between pattern-geometry strength and task accuracy. It does not directly quantify pairwise model-to-model alignment. It also compares LLM geometries with several human EEG measures; these are recorded below as findings not covered by the listed versions. Behavioral accuracy figures alone are not included as representation-alignment results.
record.test_reason: The study never compares models' representations with each other. Each LLM's layer RDM is correlated with a hand-built task-category reference RDM, and LLM RDMs are compared with human EEG RDMs. Matching a task design matrix, and its link to accuracy, is a related but different construct from cross-model alignment. The authors only cite the Platonic Representation Hypothesis as consistent with their observation. No pairwise model-to-model similarity, size sweep, mapping, seed or feature analysis is reported, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors call the FRP correlations 'moderate' rather than modest. They conclude that every LLM clusters abstract pattern categories in intermediate layers, with clustering strength scaling with performance. They read the non-significant but systematic FRP correspondence as preliminary evidence of a shared representational space with human brains. They also say mid-layer RDMs of all models 'converged on a remarkably similar geometry,' citing the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, but they did not quantify model-to-model similarity.
record.recipe_differences: Uses RSA against a task-defined pattern reference and human EEG RDMs; it does not directly measure pairwise alignment among models or sweep alignment against model size.
record.method_sensitivity: The human-to-model RSA outcome differed by EEG measure: FRP correlations were positive and larger than response-ERP and resting-EEG correlations; the FRP correlations were not permutation-significant.

fits_no_version.finding: In all eight LLMs, similarity to a task-category reference RDM follows an inverted U across layers, peaking near 47.5% depth. Peak similarity correlates with task accuracy (r = .71).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Across LLM families and sizes, intermediate layers encode abstract task-category structure, and more accurate models encode it more strongly.

fits_no_version.finding: Task-optimal LLM RDMs correlate positively but non-significantly with human frontal FRP RDMs (r ≈ .17–.25), and more strongly than with response-ERP or resting-EEG RDMs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLM representations of abstract patterns weakly align with fixation-locked human frontal EEG geometry.

record.problems: The study does not directly quantify pairwise model-to-model alignment or test its relationship with model size. The human EEG sample contains 25 participants, and none of the reported LLM–EEG correlations reached permutation significance. The authors also note a mismatch between the human visuospatial task and the LLM text presentation.
record.rows_left_out: Behavioral accuracy results by model and pattern type were not included because they do not themselves measure representation alignment; the aggregate accuracy–geometry association is included in R2.

untested.parts: Whole version: no pairwise alignment between models and no alignment-vs-size analysis. Models differ in family and size but are only compared to a design RDM.
Whole version: no vision–language paired data.
Whole version: no mapping or stitching.
Whole version: no feature or circuit analysis.
Whole version: a single metric (correlation distance with Pearson RSA) on a single task.
Whole version: no analysis of alignment ceiling or causes.

missing.what: Per-model peak similarity to the reference RDM. It is shown only graphically, but would allow a size trend of task-structure encoding (not cross-model alignment) to be read off.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 'supports' label is removed: convergence toward a task design matrix is not measured cross-model alignment. The convergence statement is an interpretive aside backed only by the grand-average RDM and the design-RDM correlations.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not directly compare pairwise model-to-model distances, test whether alignment rises with model size, or compare models across different objectives, training data, or modalities.
No paired image-caption vision-language model comparison.
No same-architecture models trained from different initializations or shared-subspace analysis.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test.
No analysis of recurring interpretable features or circuits.
No comparison of representation-similarity metrics, settings such as neighbour count, or in-distribution versus out-of-distribution inputs.
The study does not test whether shared training data or objectives explain cross-model alignment, or whether alignment plateaus or remains incomplete.

rows.subject: All eight open-source LLMs (aggregate)
rows.size_stated: 2B, 3B, 9B, 14B, 27B, 70B, and 72B models; aggregate across eight models
rows.stage_stated: mixed; includes instruct models and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B
rows.operation_detail: Layer-wise RSA against the reference RDM encoding abstract-pattern categories

conditions.value: Pearson correlation between layer RDM and reference RDM

rows.measure: Layer-wise similarity to the task-pattern reference geometry
rows.baseline: Reference RDM assigns 0 to within-pattern pairs and 1 to between-pattern pairs
rows.value: For every LLM, similarity was negligible in early layers, rose to an intermediate-layer peak, then tapered toward the output; peak depth averaged 47.52% of model depth (SD = 13.17%).
rows.locator: Results, Identification of task-optimal LLM layer; Figure 5
rows.note: The text also says the task-optimal RDMs from every model clustered trials by abstract-pattern class. No model-specific peak correlation values are stated in the text.
rows.check: Measures each model's similarity to a task-defined reference RDM, not alignment between models. It cannot show whether independently trained models converge with one another or with scale.

rows.subject: All eight open-source LLMs (aggregate)
rows.size_stated: 2B, 3B, 9B, 14B, 27B, 70B, and 72B models; aggregate across eight models
rows.stage_stated: mixed; includes instruct models and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B
rows.operation_detail: Association of task accuracy with maximum layer similarity to the reference RDM
rows.measure: Pearson correlation between overall accuracy and maximum similarity to the reference RDM
rows.locator: Results, Identification of task-optimal LLM layer
rows.note: This is an aggregate association across the eight models; it does not report a model-size versus alignment analysis.
rows.check: The accuracy vs. maximum reference-similarity correlation (r = .71) concerns task-structure encoding versus capability, not cross-model alignment. The reported 'SD = .03' on a single correlation across eight models is unexplained in the text.

rows.note: The authors state that none of the LLM–EEG correlations reached permutation significance. This human-to-model comparison is not a measure of alignment between independently trained models.
rows.check: LLM–human EEG comparison, not model–model alignment. Correctly unlinked.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: The eight tested LLMs on the abstract-pattern task
reader_labels.reason: All models showed intermediate-layer organization by pattern class, and the strength of geometry relative to the task reference was positively associated with accuracy (R1–R2); the study does not establish size-dependent pairwise model alignment.
